subject: Error requiring simulation function for user-defined distribution

messages.author: 94c2ffcec4dc149d
messages.subject: Error requiring simulation function for user-defined distribution
parts:
I am exploring how to use user-defined distributions, and am starting with the example in the manual (chapter 12.2), which defines dmyexp().

After the definition of dmyexp(), but not rmyexp(), I have the following model code:

code <- nimbleCode({
y ~ dmyexp(x)

# priors
x ~ dunif(0,1)
})

constants <- list()
data <- list(y=0)
initial_values <- list(x=0.5)

nimbleMCMC(code=code,
constants=constants,
data=data,
inits=initial_values)

The result is the following error message:

Compiling
[Note] This may take a minute.
[Note] Use 'showCompilerOutput = TRUE' to see C++ compilation details.
Error: In sizeAssignAfterRecursing: 'rmyexp' is not available or its output type is unknown. This may occur if a user-defined function name is the same as the name of a function in a package that `nimble` uses.
This occurred for: model_y[1] <<- rmyexp(=1,rate=model_x[1])
This was part of the call: {
model_y[1] <<- rmyexp(=1,rate=model_x[1])
}
Execution halted

I am not understanding where there is a need for the simulation function rmyexp(), because to my eyes everything seems initialized.

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks a lot.

Cheers,
Brook

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Error requiring simulation function for user-defined distribution
parts:
Brook, this is a good question.  The automatic registration of distributions should have handled this, but you're correct that it doesn't.

When a custom-written distribution is "registered" in nimble (allowing it to be used in a model), nimble checks for the density function (the d-function), and also looks for the random generation function (the r-function).  If it doesn't find the random generation function, then it creates one for you (which won't operate correctly, but it's a placeholder), and then registers them for use.

When you jump right into calling nimbleMCMC, this registration does take place, but something is going awry with the generation of (or more possible, the location of) the random generation function.  This is something we'll have to look into.

In the meantime, just manually registering your dmyexp distribution (before calling nimbleMCMC) will take care of this for you:

registerDistributions('dmyexp')

Let me know if this works ok for you.

Cheers!
Daniel

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Error requiring simulation function for user-defined distribution
parts:
Good question - it's not an issue of "needing to call the r-function", but rather "the nimble compiler being able to find the r-function".

Neither way (manual registration, or automatic-registration) is trying to *call* the r-function.  However, when the r-function is being created by the "automatic-registration", I believe it's being created in a location that the compiler can't find.
